title: A Benchmark for Early-stage Parkinson's Disease Detection from Speech
summary: Early-stage Parkinson's disease (EarlyPD) detection from speech is clinically meaningful yet underexplored, and published results are hard to compare because studies differ in datasets, languages, tasks, evaluation protocols, and EarlyPD definitions. To address this issue, we propose the first benchmark for speech-based EarlyPD detection, with a speaker-independent split designed for fair and replicable cross-method evaluation on researcher-accessible datasets. The benchmark covers three common speech tasks and evaluates methods under different training-resource settings. We also present multi-dimensional evaluation breakdowns by dataset, aggregation level, gender, and disease stage to support fine-grained comparisons and clinical adoption. Our results provide a replicable reference and actionable insights, encouraging the adoption of this publicly available benchmark to advance robust and clinically meaningful EarlyPD detection from speech.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes the first benchmark for speech-based early-stage Parkinson's disease (EarlyPD) detection, addressing issues of non-comparability across prior studies. It covers three speech tasks with speaker-independent splits, multiple training-resource settings, and fine-grained evaluation breakdowns (dataset, gender, disease stage) to enable fair, replicable comparisons and support clinical adoption.
AI.motivation: EarlyPD detection from speech is clinically important but underexplored, and existing results are incomparable due to differences in datasets, languages, tasks, evaluation protocols, and EarlyPD definitions. A standardized benchmark is needed to enable fair and replicable cross-method evaluation.
AI.method: The benchmark uses speaker-independent splits for fair evaluation on researcher-accessible datasets, covers three common speech tasks, evaluates methods under various training-resource settings, and provides multi-dimensional evaluation breakdowns by dataset, aggregation level, gender, and disease stage.
AI.result: Results offer a replicable reference and actionable insights for EarlyPD detection from speech, with detailed comparisons across fine-grained evaluation dimensions.
AI.conclusion: The authors encourage adoption of this publicly available benchmark to advance robust and clinically meaningful EarlyPD detection from speech.

title: SpeakerLLM: A Speaker-Specialized Audio-LLM for Speaker Understanding and Verification Reasoning
summary: As audio-first agents become increasingly common in physical AI, conversational robots, and screenless wearables, audio large language models (audio-LLMs) must integrate speaker-specific understanding to support user authorization, personalization, and context-aware interaction. This requires modeling who is speaking, how the voice sounds, and how recording conditions affect speaker cues. Conventional speaker verification systems provide strong scalar scores but little linguistic evidence, while current audio-LLMs and speaker-aware language models have limited ability to organize speaker information beyond binary labels or descriptive profiles. We present SpeakerLLM, a speaker-specialized audio-LLM framework that unifies single-utterance speaker profiling, recording-condition understanding, utterance-pair speaker comparison, and evidence-organized verification reasoning within a natural-language interface. We construct verification-reasoning targets and a decision-composition policy that separate profile-level evidence from the final same-or-different decision and organize recording condition, profile evidence, and the decision into a structured trace. At its core, SpeakerLLM uses a hierarchical speaker tokenizer designed to capture multiple granularities of speaker evidence. Utterance-level speaker embeddings summarize identity and profile-level cues, whereas frame-level speaker features preserve fine-grained acoustic descriptors. Experiments show that SpeakerLLM-Base improves speaker-profile and recording-condition understanding over general audio-LLMs, while SpeakerLLM-VR preserves strong generated-verdict accuracy and produces decision traces grounded in the supervised verification reasoning schema. We will release the metadata-enriched supervision dataset and target-construction code for reproducibility.

AI.tldr: SpeakerLLM is a speaker-specialized audio-LLM framework that unifies speaker profiling, recording-condition understanding, speaker comparison, and evidence-organized verification reasoning using a hierarchical speaker tokenizer and a structured decision-composition policy.
AI.motivation: Audio-LLMs lack integrated speaker-specific understanding for authorization, personalization, and context-aware interaction; conventional speaker verification provides scalar scores without linguistic evidence, and existing models cannot organize speaker information beyond binary labels or descriptive profiles.
AI.method: SpeakerLLM framework with (1) hierarchical speaker tokenizer capturing utterance-level embeddings (identity/profile cues) and frame-level features (fine-grained acoustic descriptors), (2) verification-reasoning targets and decision-composition policy separating profile-level evidence from final same-or-different decision, (3) structured trace organizing recording condition, profile evidence, and decision.
AI.result: SpeakerLLM-Base improves speaker-profile and recording-condition understanding over general audio-LLMs; SpeakerLLM-VR preserves strong generated-verdict accuracy with decision traces grounded in supervised verification reasoning schema.
AI.conclusion: Unified speaker-specialized audio-LLM framework enables interpretable, evidence-grounded speaker verification and profiling within a natural-language interface, with plans to release supervision dataset and code for reproducibility.

title: Masked Autoencoders with Limited Data: Does It Work? A Fine-Grained Bioacoustics Case Study
comment: Workshop on Fine-Grained Visual Categorization (FGVC) at CVPR 2026. 8 pages, 6 figures
summary: Bioacoustic recognition requires fine-grained acoustic understanding to distinguish similar-sounding species. However, many large-scale data repositories such as iNaturalist are weakly annotated, often with only a single positive species label per recording, making supervised learning particularly challenging. Inspired by advances in computer vision, recent approaches have shifted toward self-supervised learning to capture the underlying structure of audio without relying on exhaustive annotations. In particular, masked autoencoders (MAE) have shown strong transferability on massive audio corpora, yet their effectiveness in more modest bioacoustic settings remains underexplored. In this work, we conduct a systematic study of MAE pretraining for species classification on iNatSounds, analyzing the impacts of pretraining data scale, domain specificity, data curation, and transfer strategies. Consistent with prior work, we find that models pretrained on diverse general audio data achieve the best transfer performance on iNatSounds. Contrary to observations from large-scale audio benchmarks, we find that (1) additional masked reconstruction pretraining on domain-specific data provides limited benefits and may even degrade performance relative to off-the-shelf models, and (2) selective data filtering offers a negligible advantage when the overall data scale is limited. Our results indicate that, in moderate-sized fine-grained bioacoustic settings, pretraining scale dominates objective design. These findings further clarify when MAE-based pretraining is effective and provide practical guidance for model selection under limited supervision.

AI.tldr: This paper systematically evaluates masked autoencoder (MAE) pretraining for fine-grained species classification on the iNatSounds bioacoustic dataset, finding that diverse general audio pretraining dominates domain-specific pretraining and data curation when data scale is limited.
AI.motivation: Bioacoustic recognition requires fine-grained audio understanding, but large-scale repositories like iNaturalist are weakly annotated (single positive label per recording), making supervised learning challenging. The effectiveness of MAE pretraining in modest bioacoustic settings is underexplored.
AI.method: Systematic study of MAE pretraining for species classification on iNatSounds, analyzing impacts of pretraining data scale, domain specificity, data curation, and transfer strategies.
AI.result: (1) Models pretrained on diverse general audio data achieve the best transfer performance; (2) additional masked reconstruction pretraining on domain-specific data offers limited benefits and may degrade performance; (3) selective data filtering provides negligible advantage when data scale is limited.
AI.conclusion: In moderate-sized fine-grained bioacoustic settings, pretraining scale dominates objective design. The findings clarify when MAE-based pretraining is effective and provide practical guidance for model selection under limited supervision.

title: Refining Pseudo-Audio Prompts with Speech-Text Alignment for Text-Only Domain Adaptation in LLM-Based ASR
summary: LLM-based automatic speech recognition models demonstrate strong performance by connecting audio encoders and LLMs. However, data scarcity of paired speech and transcription often hinders their adaptation to new domains, making text-only domain adaptation crucial. Existing methods typically rely on either fine-tuning the LLM alone or employing pseudo-audio prompts. The former neglects essential acoustic context, while the latter either suffers from limited scalability in data-scarce conditions, or yields inexpressive prompts by leveraging only textual features, ignoring audio modality. To address this, we propose an enhanced framework that explicitly models speech-text alignment. Our method efficiently generates highly expressive pseudo-audio prompts that bridges the modality gap, enabling effective target-domain adaptation. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing text-only methods, improving both overall error rates and out-of-vocabulary coverage.

AI.tldr: Proposes an enhanced text-only domain adaptation framework for LLM-based ASR that generates expressive pseudo-audio prompts by explicitly modeling speech-text alignment, outperforming existing methods on error rates and OOV coverage.
AI.motivation: Data scarcity of paired speech-transcription data hinders adaptation of LLM-based ASR to new domains; existing text-only methods either neglect acoustic context or produce inexpressive prompts that fail to bridge the modality gap.
AI.method: An enhanced framework that explicitly models speech-text alignment to efficiently generate highly expressive pseudo-audio prompts, bridging the modality gap between text-only inputs and audio representations for target-domain adaptation.
AI.result: Outperforms existing text-only domain adaptation methods, improving overall error rates and out-of-vocabulary (OOV) coverage.
AI.conclusion: Explicitly modeling speech-text alignment for pseudo-audio prompt generation is an effective strategy for text-only domain adaptation in LLM-based ASR, surpassing approaches that fine-tune LLM alone or use less expressive prompts.

title: Receding Horizon Multi-Agent Deceptive Path Planner
summary: Deceptive path planning enables autonomous agents to obscure their true goals from observers by deviating from an expected optimal path. Prior work largely solves full-horizon, end-to-end optimization for single agents, which is expensive to recompute online and difficult to scale or adapt en route. We propose a unified framework for deceptive path planning using a Boltzmann distribution, computing over short-horizon candidate trajectories within a receding-horizon loop. By param- By iterating a user-defined cost that captures deception, resources, and smoothness, and optionally includes coupling terms between agents, the framework yields stochastic policies that balance the tradeoff between optimal paths and deceptive deviation. Policies are updated locally and do not require training. The level of deception and adherence to constraints can be dynamically tuned, enabling online adaptation to changes in goals and constraints such as obstacles. This step-by-step tuning opens the door to new forms of dynamic deception. Simulation studies demonstrate the flexibility of our approach, maintaining deception while adapting to environmental and constraint updates, avoiding the recomputation required by full-horizon methods, and supporting intuitive tuning via a small set of parameters

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a receding-horizon deceptive path planning framework using a Boltzmann distribution over short-horizon candidate trajectories, enabling online adaptation and multi-agent scalability without full-horizon recomputation.
AI.motivation: Prior deceptive path planning methods rely on full-horizon, end-to-end optimization for single agents, which is computationally expensive to recompute online and difficult to scale or adapt dynamically during execution.
AI.method: The framework uses a Boltzmann distribution to compute stochastic policies over short-horizon candidate trajectories within a receding-horizon loop. A user-defined cost function captures deception, resource efficiency, smoothness, and optionally inter-agent coupling. Policies are updated locally without training, and deception/constraint adherence levels are tunable via a small parameter set.
AI.result: Simulation studies show the approach maintains deception while adapting to environmental and constraint changes, avoids full-horizon recomputation, and supports intuitive parameter-based tuning.
AI.conclusion: The framework enables online, scalable deceptive path planning with dynamic tunability, opening doors to new forms of dynamic deception in multi-agent settings.

title: Physics-Based iOCT Sonification for Real-time Interaction Awareness in Subretinal Injection
summary: Subretinal injection is a delicate vitreoretinal procedure requiring precise needle placement within the subretinal space while avoiding perforation of the retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), a layer directly beneath the target with extremely limited regenerative capacity. To enhance depth perception during cannula advancement, intraoperative optical coherence tomography (iOCT) offers high-resolution cross-sectional visualization of needle-tissue interaction; however, interpreting these images requires sustained visual attention alongside the en face microscope view, thereby increasing cognitive load during critical phases and placing additional demands on the surgeon's proprioceptive control. In this paper, we propose a structured, real-time sonification framework designed for extensible mapping of iOCT-derived anatomical features into perceptual auditory feedback. The method employs a physics-inspired acoustic model driven by segmented retinal layers from a stream of iOCT B-scans, with needle motion and injection-induced retinal layer displacements serving as excitation inputs to the sound model, enabling perception of tool position and retinal deformation. In a controlled user study (n=34), the proposed sonification achieved high retinal layer identification accuracy and robust detection of retinal deformation-related events, significantly outperforming a state-of-the-art baseline in overall event identification (83.4% vs. 60.6%, p < 0.001), with gains driven primarily by enhanced detection of injection-induced retinal deformation. Evaluation by experts (n=4) confirmed the clinical relevance and potential intraoperative applicability of the method. These results establish structured iOCT sonification as a viable complementary modality for real-time surgical guidance in subretinal injection.

AI.tldr: A real-time sonification framework using iOCT-derived data to convert retinal layer features into auditory feedback significantly improved event detection accuracy (83.4% vs. 60.6%) during subretinal injection, reducing cognitive load on surgeons.
AI.motivation: Subretinal injection requires precise needle placement near the RPE layer with limited regenerative capacity. iOCT provides cross-sectional visualization but increases cognitive load by requiring surgeons to divide attention between en face and OCT views during critical phases.
AI.method: A structured real-time sonification framework using a physics-inspired acoustic model driven by segmented retinal layers from iOCT B-scans, with needle motion and injection-induced retinal layer displacements as excitation inputs to generate auditory feedback for tool position and retinal deformation perception.
AI.result: In a user study (n=34), the sonification achieved 83.4% overall event identification accuracy vs. 60.6% baseline (p<0.001), with gains primarily from enhanced detection of injection-induced retinal deformation. Expert evaluation (n=4) confirmed clinical relevance.
AI.conclusion: Structured iOCT sonification is a viable complementary modality for real-time surgical guidance in subretinal injection, offering a way to reduce cognitive load while improving perceptual accuracy during delicate retinal procedures.

title: Frequency Nadir-Constrained Power System Restoration Planning with Energy Storage
summary: Power system restoration following blackouts must ensure frequency stability throughout the recovery process. This paper proposes a frequency-constrained mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) framework for black-start restoration planning in transmission systems with synchronous machines and energy storage systems. To prevent excessive frequency deviations caused by restorative actions, a frequency nadir prediction method is developed for power systems with energy storage system (ESS) integration and incorporated into a multiperiod optimization framework. The formulation ensures that frequency deviations resulting from restorative actions remain within prescribed safe limits. Furthermore, the presented framework leverages ESSs to enhance frequency security and recovery speed. Case studies on a modified IEEE 9-bus system demonstrate that the computed restoration plan maintains frequency security, as validated through MATLAB and PSS/E simulations, while reducing restoration time through ESS coordination.

AI.tldr: A frequency-constrained MILP framework is proposed for black-start restoration planning in transmission systems with synchronous machines and energy storage systems, using a frequency nadir prediction method to ensure frequency deviations stay within safe limits and leveraging ESSs to enhance frequency security and recovery speed.
AI.motivation: Power system restoration after blackouts must maintain frequency stability, and existing methods lack integration of frequency security constraints with energy storage systems for black-start planning.
AI.method: Develops a frequency nadir prediction method for systems with ESS integration, incorporates it into a multiperiod MILP optimization framework, and validates through MATLAB and PSS/E simulations on a modified IEEE 9-bus system.
AI.result: The computed restoration plan maintains frequency security within prescribed limits and reduces restoration time through ESS coordination, as validated by simulations.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework effectively ensures frequency security during black-start restoration and leverages ESS to accelerate the recovery process.

title: Break-the-Beat! Controllable MIDI-to-Drum Audio Synthesis
summary: Current methods for creating drum loop audio in digital music production, such as using one-shot samples or resampling, often demand non-trivial efforts of creators. While recent generative models achieve high fidelity and adhere to text, they lack the specific control needed for such a task. Existing symbolic-to-audio research often focuses on single, tonal instruments, leaving the challenge of polyphonic, percussive drum synthesis unaddressed. We address this gap by introducing ``Break-the-Beat!,'' a model capable of rendering a drum MIDI with the timbre of a reference audio. It is built by fine-tuning a pre-trained text-to-audio model with our proposed content encoder and a effective hybrid conditioning mechanism. To enable this, we construct a new dataset of paired target-reference drum audio from existing drum audio datasets. Experiments demonstrate that our model generates high-quality drum audio that follows high-resolution drum MIDI, achieving strong performance across metrics of audio quality, rhythmic alignment, and beat continuity. This offer producers a new, controllable tool for creative production. Demo page: https://ik4sumii.github.io/break-the-beat/

AI.tldr: Break-the-Beat is a model that renders drum MIDI with the timbre of a reference audio by fine-tuning a pre-trained text-to-audio model with a content encoder and hybrid conditioning mechanism, achieving high-quality drum audio with strong rhythmic alignment and beat continuity.
AI.motivation: Current drum loop creation methods (one-shot samples, resampling) require significant manual effort, and existing generative models lack fine-grained control for polyphonic percussive drum synthesis. Prior symbolic-to-audio work mainly focuses on single tonal instruments, leaving drum synthesis unexplored.
AI.method: The model fine-tunes a pre-trained text-to-audio model with a proposed content encoder and a hybrid conditioning mechanism. A new dataset of paired target-reference drum audio is constructed from existing drum audio datasets.
AI.result: The model generates high-quality drum audio following high-resolution drum MIDI, achieving strong performance in audio quality, rhythmic alignment, and beat continuity.
AI.conclusion: Break-the-Beat offers producers a new controllable tool for creative drum production, bridging the gap between symbolic drum patterns and expressive audio rendering.

title: JAX-Based Batched AC Power Flow for GPU Acceleration and AI Ecosystem Integration
comment: In review for IEEE POWER ENGINEERING LETTERS
summary: Coordinating growing grid flexibility under uncertainty is becoming increasingly important for efficient and reliable power-system operation. A core computational requirement is the efficient large-scale batched evaluation of AC power flow across candidate operating actions and uncertainty scenarios. Previous work has explored GPU-based batched power-flow evaluation, but has largely relied on hand-written C or CUDA code, creating barriers to customisation, efficient kernel optimisation, and long-term maintenance. JAX is a Python-based framework that enables efficient accelerator execution while keeping implementations in Python. This letter therefore proposes a JAX-based batched AC power-flow solver that uses current JAX functionality to implement Newton--Raphson for transmission networks and Z-Bus power flow for three-phase unbalanced distribution networks, achieving more than 10x speed-ups relative to pandapower and OpenDSS. In addition, JAX integrates seamlessly with the broader JAX-based AI ecosystem, making it straightforward to embed power-flow evaluation within AI methods for future larger-scale and more complex power-system operation.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a JAX-based batched AC power-flow solver that achieves 10x speed-ups over traditional tools (pandapower, OpenDSS) by leveraging GPU acceleration for Newton-Raphson (transmission) and Z-Bus (distribution) methods, with seamless integration into the JAX AI ecosystem.
AI.motivation: Coordinating growing grid flexibility under uncertainty demands efficient batched AC power-flow evaluation across many operating actions and scenarios, but existing GPU solutions rely on hand-written C/CUDA code that hinders customization, optimization, and maintenance.
AI.method: A JAX-based batched AC power-flow solver implementing Newton-Raphson for transmission networks and Z-Bus power flow for three-phase unbalanced distribution networks, leveraging JAX's automatic differentiation, JIT compilation, and GPU acceleration while keeping the implementation in Python.
AI.result: Achieves more than 10x speed-ups relative to pandapower and OpenDSS for batched power-flow evaluations.
AI.conclusion: JAX-based power-flow solver provides efficient GPU-accelerated batched evaluation with Python-native code, and integrates seamlessly with the JAX AI ecosystem for embedding within AI methods for future large-scale power-system operation.

title: IsoNet: Spatially-aware audio-visual target speech extraction in complex acoustic environments
summary: Target speech extraction remains difficult for compact devices because monaural neural models lack spatial evidence and classical beamformers lose resolving power when the microphone aperture is only a few centimetres. We present IsoNet, a user-selectable audio-visual target speech extraction system for a compact 4-microphone array. IsoNet combines complex multi-channel STFT features, GCC-PHAT spatial cues, face-conditioned visual embeddings, and auxiliary direction-of-arrival supervision inside a U-Net mask estimation network. Three curriculum variants were trained on 25,000 simulated VoxCeleb mixtures with progressively difficult SNR regimes. On a hard test set spanning -1 to 10 dB SNR, IsoNet-CL1 achieves 9.31 dB SI-SDR, a 4.85 dB improvement over the mixture, with PESQ 2.13 and STOI 0.84. Oracle delay-and-sum and MVDR beamformers degrade the same mixtures by 4.82 dB and 6.08 dB SI-SDRi, respectively, showing that the proposed learned multimodal conditioning solves a regime where conventional spatial filtering is ineffective. Ablation studies show consistent gains from visual conditioning, GCC-PHAT features, and extended delay-bin encoding. The results establish a compact-array, face-selectable speech extraction baseline under controlled simulation and identify the remaining barriers to real deployment, especially phase reconstruction, multi-interferer mixtures, and simulation-to-real transfer.

AI.tldr: IsoNet is a multimodal (audio-visual) target speech extraction system designed for compact 4-microphone arrays. It combines complex STFT, GCC-PHAT, face embeddings, and DOA supervision in a U-Net. On hard test sets (-1 to 10 dB SNR), it achieves 9.31 dB SI-SDR (4.85 dB improvement) and significantly outperforms classical beamformers (delay-and-sum, MVDR) which degrade performance. Ablations confirm gains from visual, GCC-PHAT, and delay-bin encoding. The paper establishes a baseline while noting barriers to real deployment: phase reconstruction, multi-interferer mixtures, and sim-to-real transfer.
AI.motivation: Target speech extraction on compact devices is challenging because monaural neural models lack spatial cues, and classical beamformers lose effectiveness when the microphone aperture is only a few centimetres. The authors aim to solve this by leveraging multimodal (audio-visual) information.
AI.method: IsoNet integrates complex multi-channel STFT features, GCC-PHAT spatial cues, face-conditioned visual embeddings, and auxiliary direction-of-arrival (DOA) supervision within a U-Net mask estimation network. Three curriculum variants (CL1-CL3) are trained on 25,000 simulated VoxCeleb mixtures with progressively difficult SNR regimes.
AI.result: On a hard test set (-1 to 10 dB SNR), IsoNet-CL1 achieves 9.31 dB SI-SDR (4.85 dB improvement over mixture), PESQ 2.13, STOI 0.84. Oracle delay-and-sum and MVDR beamformers degrade SI-SDRi by 4.82 dB and 6.08 dB respectively, showing the proposed method solves regimes where conventional beamforming fails.
AI.conclusion: The learned multimodal conditioning approach effectively solves target speech extraction for compact arrays where classical beamforming is ineffective. Ablations confirm consistent gains from visual conditioning, GCC-PHAT features, and extended delay-bin encoding. Remaining barriers for real deployment include phase reconstruction, multi-interferer scenarios, and simulation-to-real transfer.

title: Battery-Assisted Operation of Hyperscale AI Data Centers under Connect-and-Manage Interconnection Practices
summary: Emerging connect-and-manage practices allow new transmission-connected mega-loads to connect while enforcing time-varying admissible power exchange limits at the point of common coupling (PCC) in real time. Hyperscale artificial intelligence data centers (AIDCs), whose demand can reach hundreds of megawatts and whose internal computing-cooling dynamics evolve rapidly, can therefore face frequent conflicts between workload continuity requirements and externally imposed PCC envelopes. This paper proposes a battery-assisted operational framework in which on-site battery energy storage (BESS) serves as a physical buffering interface to reconcile fast internal dynamics with time-varying interconnection limits. A continuity-aware energy-computation model is developed to jointly capture checkpoint-constrained AI training workloads, information technology (IT) computing power-throughput characteristics, and IT-cooling thermal dynamics. A two-stage decision framework is then formulated, consisting of scenario-based day-ahead workload commitment and a real-time receding-horizon delivery assurance controller that enforces battery, thermal, and grid-interaction constraints. Case studies on the IEEE 39-bus system with Australian real data demonstrate that BESS substantially increases credible day-ahead workload commitment and improves real-time delivery robustness under transmission congestion. Sensitivity analyses further reveal a regime-dependent role transition of BESS -- from feasibility-oriented continuity support when PCC limits are binding to economy-driven flexibility provision as transmission constraints are relaxed.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a battery-assisted operational framework for hyperscale AI data centers facing time-varying grid interconnection limits, using on-site BESS as a physical buffering interface. It develops a continuity-aware energy-computation model and a two-stage decision framework (day-ahead commitment + real-time receding-horizon control). Case studies on the IEEE 39-bus system with Australian data show BESS increases workload commitment and improves delivery robustness, with a regime-dependent role transition from continuity support to economic flexibility.
AI.motivation: Emerging connect-and-manage practices impose time-varying admissible power exchange limits at PCC, causing frequent conflicts between workload continuity requirements of hyperscale AI data centers (with rapid computing-cooling dynamics) and externally imposed grid constraints.
AI.method: A battery-assisted operational framework with on-site BESS as a physical buffering interface; a continuity-aware energy-computation model capturing checkpoint-constrained AI training workloads, IT computing power-throughput characteristics, and IT-cooling thermal dynamics; a two-stage decision framework with scenario-based day-ahead workload commitment and real-time receding-horizon delivery assurance controller enforcing battery, thermal, and grid-interaction constraints.
AI.result: Case studies on IEEE 39-bus with Australian real data show BESS substantially increases credible day-ahead workload commitment and improves real-time delivery robustness under transmission congestion. Sensitivity analyses reveal a regime-dependent role transition of BESS from feasibility-oriented continuity support (when PCC limits are binding) to economy-driven flexibility provision (when transmission constraints are relaxed).
AI.conclusion: On-site BESS effectively reconciles fast internal AIDC dynamics with time-varying interconnection limits, serving dual roles depending on transmission constraint regimes, and enhances both workload commitment and operational robustness.

title: Persian MusicGen: A Large-Scale Dataset and Culturally-Aware Generative Model for Persian Music
summary: Persian music, with its unique tonalities, modal systems (Dastgah), and rhythmic structures, presents significant challenges for music generation models trained primarily on Western music. We address this gap by curating the first large-scale dataset of Persian songs, comprising over 900 hours high-quality audio samples across diverse sub-genres, including pop, traditional, and contemporary styles. This dataset captures the rich melodic and cultural diversity of Persian music and serves as the foundation for fine-tuning MusicGen, a state-of-the-art generative music model. We adapt MusicGen to this domain and evaluate its performance by utilizing subjective and objective metrics. To assess the semantic alignment between generated music and intended style tags, we report the proportion of relevant tags accurately reflected in the generated outputs. Our results demonstrate that the fine-tuned model produces compositions that more align with Persian stylistic conventions. This work introduces a new resource for generative music research and illustrates the adaptability of music generation models to underrepresented cultural and linguistic contexts.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces the first large-scale Persian music dataset (900+ hours) and fine-tunes MusicGen on it, demonstrating improved stylistic alignment with Persian musical conventions.
AI.motivation: Persian music's unique tonalities, modal systems (Dastgah), and rhythmic structures are poorly served by music generation models trained on Western music; there is a lack of large-scale Persian music datasets.
AI.method: Curated a 900+ hour Persian song dataset across pop, traditional, and contemporary genres; fine-tuned MusicGen on this dataset; evaluated using subjective metrics, objective metrics, and semantic tag alignment.
AI.result: The fine-tuned model produces compositions that better align with Persian stylistic conventions, with improved semantic alignment between generated music and intended style tags.
AI.conclusion: This work provides a new resource for generative music research and demonstrates the adaptability of music generation models to underrepresented cultural and linguistic contexts.

title: Grid Integration of Gigawatt-Scale AI Data Centers under Connect-and-Manage
summary: Emerging connect-and-manage interconnection practices allow gigawatt-scale artificial intelligence data centers (AIDCs) to connect to the transmission network without prior network upgrades, at the cost of real-time curtailment during grid stress. This paper formalizes the resulting AIDC-transmission system operator (TSO) coordination as a sequential request-acceptance protocol with an explicit curtailment variable and a strict information boundary between the two parties. Physical models are developed on both sides of the point of common coupling: the AIDC is decomposed into frontier training, batch training, and inference serving subclasses sharing on-site battery energy storage, capturing differentiated temporal flexibility; the transmission network is modeled via DC power flow with generator constraints and budget-constrained demand uncertainty. Because the TSO's acceptance mapping is opaque to the AIDC, a three-layer hierarchical architecture is formulated in which a learning-based planning layer generates power requests, the TSO evaluates each request through a robust acceptance mechanism, and a single-step execution optimizer enforces internal feasibility under the realized power budget. Case studies with a gigawatt-scale AIDC on the IEEE 39-bus system with Australian market data show that the framework reduces curtailment from 9.1% to 2.8% while preserving 98.1% frontier training workload, that batch training acts as the primary grid-elastic resource with the largest throughput swing during peak demand, and that the on-site battery provides curtailment buffering through active discharge and charge deferral.

AI.tldr: This paper formalizes coordination between gigawatt-scale AI data centers (AIDCs) and transmission system operators (TSOs) under connect-and-manage interconnection practices. It proposes a three-layer hierarchical framework with learning-based planning, robust TSO acceptance, and single-step execution, reducing curtailment from 9.1% to 2.8% while preserving 98.1% frontier training workload on the IEEE 39-bus system.
AI.motivation: Emerging connect-and-manage practices allow large AIDCs to connect to the grid without prior upgrades but subject to real-time curtailment. There is a need to formalize the AIDC-TSO coordination under strict information boundaries and develop methods to minimize curtailment while preserving critical AI workloads.
AI.method: A sequential request-acceptance protocol with explicit curtailment variable and strict information boundary. Physical models decompose AIDC into frontier training, batch training, and inference serving subclasses sharing on-site battery storage. A three-layer hierarchical architecture: learning-based planning layer generates power requests, robust TSO acceptance mechanism evaluates requests, and single-step execution optimizer enforces internal feasibility.
AI.result: Curtailment reduced from 9.1% to 2.8%; 98.1% frontier training workload preserved; batch training identified as primary grid-elastic resource; on-site battery provides curtailment buffering via active discharge and charge deferral.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework effectively coordinates AIDC-TSO interaction under connect-and-manage practices, significantly reducing curtailment while maintaining high-priority workload execution, with differentiated roles for each workload subclass and battery storage.

title: PROCESS-2: A Benchmark Speech Corpus for Early Cognitive Impairment Detection
summary: Speech-based analysis offers a scalable and non-invasive approach for detecting cognitive decline, yet progress has been constrained by the limited availability of clinically validated datasets collected under realistic conditions. We introduce PROCESS-2, a large-scale speech dataset designed to support research on automatic assessment of cognitive impairment from spontaneous and task-oriented speech. The dataset comprises recordings from 200 healthy controls, 150 mild cognitive impairment, and 50 dementia diagnoses collected using the CognoMemory digital assessment platform. Each participant completed a single assessment session, including picture description and verbal fluency tasks, accompanied by manually verified transcripts and participant-level metadata. PROCESS-2 contains approximately 21 hours of speech audio with predefined train/test partitions. Comprehensive technical validation evaluated demographic balance, clinical consistency, recording stability, embedding-space structure, and reproducible baseline modelling performance, demonstrating clinically meaningful group separation and stable performance across modelling approaches while preserving real-world conversational variability. PROCESS-2 is released under controlled access via Hugging Face to enable responsible reuse while protecting participant privacy, providing a reproducible benchmark resource for speech-based cognitive assessment research.

AI.tldr: PROCESS-2 is a large-scale, clinically validated speech dataset (21 hours, 300 participants) for detecting cognitive impairment (healthy controls, mild cognitive impairment, dementia) via spontaneous and task-oriented speech, released under controlled access on Hugging Face to enable reproducible research.
AI.motivation: Speech-based cognitive decline detection is promising but hindered by the scarcity of large, clinically validated, realistic-condition datasets.
AI.method: Dataset includes 300 participants (200 healthy, 150 MCI, 50 dementia) recorded via the CognoMemory platform performing picture description and verbal fluency tasks; includes manually verified transcripts, metadata, and predefined train/test splits (~21 hours). Technical validation covers demographic balance, clinical consistency, recording stability, embedding-space structure, and baseline modeling reproducibility.
AI.result: Clinically meaningful group separation and stable performance across modeling approaches while preserving real-world conversational variability.
AI.conclusion: PROCESS-2 provides a reproducible benchmark resource for speech-based cognitive assessment, released under controlled access to balance reusability and participant privacy.

title: Optimizing Grid-Forming Controls using Relay-based Extremum Seeking to Enhance Transient Performance
summary: Grid-forming (GFM) inverters are essential for enhancing stability in modern power systems with high penetration of inverter-based resources (IBRs). However, their performance highly depends on control parameters tuning, particularly the active power-frequency droop coefficient. This parameter presents a trade-off among competing objectives, including damping, settling time, rate of change of frequencies (RoCoF) and frequency nadirs. This paper proposes a real-time, adaptive optimization framework based on Extremum Seeking Control (ESC) to dynamically tune the GFM droop gain. A multi-objective cost function balances conflicting performance goals such as oscillation energy, frequency nadir, RoCoF, and post-disturbance settling performance. The approach is validated through numerical simulations on a modified IEEE 68-bus system. Results demonstrate that the cost function is convex with respect to the droop parameter, justifying gradient-based optimization. Furthermore, the ESC algorithm successfully tracks the time-varying optimal droop coefficient in real-time as network conditions change, thereby ensuring robust and near-optimal system performance without requiring an analytical grid model.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a real-time adaptive optimization framework using Extremum Seeking Control (ESC) to dynamically tune the droop coefficient of grid-forming inverters, balancing competing objectives like damping, settling time, RoCoF, and frequency nadir. Validated on a modified IEEE 68-bus system, the method tracks the time-varying optimal droop gain without requiring an analytical grid model.
AI.motivation: Grid-forming inverter performance depends critically on control parameters, especially the active power-frequency droop coefficient, which involves trade-offs among damping, settling time, RoCoF, and frequency nadirs. Existing static tuning methods cannot adapt to changing network conditions.
AI.method: An Extremum Seeking Control (ESC)-based adaptive optimization framework that dynamically tunes the GFM droop gain in real-time using a multi-objective cost function balancing oscillation energy, frequency nadir, RoCoF, and post-disturbance settling performance. The method is gradient-based and model-free.
AI.result: The cost function is convex with respect to the droop parameter, justifying gradient-based optimization. The ESC algorithm successfully tracks the time-varying optimal droop coefficient in real-time under changing network conditions, ensuring robust near-optimal performance.
AI.conclusion: The proposed ESC-based framework enables real-time, model-free adaptive tuning of GFM inverter droop gains, effectively balancing multiple competing performance objectives and maintaining near-optimal stability performance as grid conditions evolve.

title: Text-Dependent Speaker Verification (TdSV) Challenge 2024: Team Naive System Report
summary: This paper presents a system for the 2024 Text-Dependent Speaker Verification (TdSV) Challenge. The system achieved a Minimum Detection Cost Function (MinDCF) of 0.0461 and an Equal Error Rate (EER) of 1.3\%. Our approach focused on adapting existing state-of-the-art neural networks, ResNet-TDNN and NeXt-TDNN, originally trained on the VoxCeleb dataset. This strategy was chosen because of the limited challenge duration and the available resources at the time. In addition, we designed a lightweight and resource-efficient model, EfficientNet-A0, trained specifically on the challenge dataset to improve adaptation and strengthen the ensemble approach. Our system combines advanced neural architectures, extensive data augmentation, and optimised hyperparameters. These components helped achieve strong performance in text-dependent speaker verification. The results also demonstrate the effectiveness of multi-model ensemble learning for both speaker and phrase verification.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a system for the 2024 Text-Dependent Speaker Verification Challenge, achieving MinDCF of 0.0461 and EER of 1.3%. It adapts pre-trained ResNet-TDNN and NeXt-TDNN models from VoxCeleb, plus a lightweight EfficientNet-A0 trained on the challenge dataset, using multi-model ensemble learning, data augmentation, and optimized hyperparameters for strong performance.
AI.motivation: To develop a competitive system for the 2024 TdSV Challenge under constraints of limited duration and resources, by adapting existing state-of-the-art speaker verification models and designing a lightweight model specifically for the challenge dataset.
AI.method: Adapted pre-trained ResNet-TDNN and NeXt-TDNN models originally trained on VoxCeleb; designed a lightweight EfficientNet-A0 trained on the challenge dataset; employed multi-model ensemble learning, extensive data augmentation, and optimized hyperparameters for speaker and phrase verification.
AI.result: Achieved MinDCF of 0.0461 and EER of 1.3% on the 2024 TdSV Challenge.
AI.conclusion: Multi-model ensemble learning combining adapted large models and a lightweight task-specific model, along with data augmentation and hyperparameter optimization, is effective for text-dependent speaker verification.

title: Day-to-Day Traffic Network Modeling under Route-Guidance Misinformation: Endogenous Trust and Resilience in CAV Environments
comment: 10 pages, 7 figures. Under review at IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Transportation Systems
summary: Connected and autonomous vehicles and smart mobility services increasingly use digital route guidance as an operational input to traffic network management. When this information becomes unreliable or adversarial, day-to-day traffic models must represent not only flow adaptation but also the evolution of user trust in the information source. This paper develops a coupled day-to-day traffic assignment and trust-evolution framework for route-guidance misinformation. Within-day congestion is represented by Lighthill-Whitham-Richards network loading, while day-to-day route choice follows bounded-rationality logit learning with trust-dependent reliance on external guidance. Trust is modeled as an aggregate class-level behavioral reliance state encoded by a Beta evidence model and updated from repeated guidance errors. Theoretical analysis establishes stationary equilibria, a conservative stability guide, a weighted compliance index for population-level vulnerability, and an asymmetric recovery law that explains post-attack trust hysteresis. Numerical experiments on Sioux Falls, with an Anaheim robustness check, show that endogenous trust creates a threshold-based resilience mechanism. Below the trust-activation threshold, the attack remains behaviorally stealthy and dynamic trust provides almost no attenuation. Above the threshold, trust erosion reduces the impact of the fixed-trust attack by about 91 percent in Sioux Falls and 85 percent in Anaheim. The experiments also show that CAV penetration increases fixed-trust vulnerability while preserving dynamic attenuation, and that traffic performance can recover before trust, resulting in a 77-day hidden vulnerability window. The results provide a trust-aware modeling basis for resilience analysis in CAV-enabled traffic networks.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a coupled day-to-day traffic assignment and trust-evolution framework for route-guidance misinformation, showing that endogenous trust creates threshold-based resilience where trust erosion reduces attack impact by ~91% (Sioux Falls) and ~85% (Anaheim), while revealing a 77-day hidden vulnerability window where traffic recovers before trust.
AI.motivation: When digital route guidance becomes unreliable or adversarial, existing day-to-day traffic models must represent not only flow adaptation but also the evolution of user trust in the information source, which is currently missing from the literature.
AI.method: Coupled day-to-day traffic assignment and trust-evolution framework using Lighthill-Whitham-Richards network loading for within-day congestion, bounded-rationality logit learning with trust-dependent reliance on external guidance for day-to-day route choice, and Beta evidence model for trust as an aggregate class-level behavioral reliance state updated from repeated guidance errors.
AI.result: Endogenous trust creates a threshold-based resilience mechanism; below the trust-activation threshold the attack is behaviorally stealthy, above it trust erosion reduces attack impact by ~91% in Sioux Falls and ~85% in Anaheim. CAV penetration increases fixed-trust vulnerability while preserving dynamic attenuation. Traffic can recover before trust, creating a 77-day hidden vulnerability window.
AI.conclusion: The results provide a trust-aware modeling basis for resilience analysis in CAV-enabled traffic networks, establishing stationary equilibria, a conservative stability guide, a weighted compliance index for population-level vulnerability, and an asymmetric recovery law explaining post-attack trust hysteresis.

title: Energy Management for Solar-Powered Electric-Bus Charging Station: A Data-Driven Method
comment: 5 pages, 4 figures. To appear in the IEEE PES General Meeting 2026
summary: This paper presents a flexible energy management system (EMS) for an electric bus charging station (EBCS) that integrates renewable generation, energy storage, and electric bus (EB) charging while accounting for uncertainties in solar PV output, electricity prices, and EB arrival/departure state of charge. A data-driven polynomial chaos expansion surrogate is developed from a limited set of uncertainty samples, and a nonparametric inference method is used to enrich the input data when historical data is limited. Case studies on a solar-powered EBCS with 20 EBs demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed EMS and data-driven method.

AI.tldr: A flexible energy management system for electric bus charging stations integrates renewable generation and storage, using a data-driven polynomial chaos expansion surrogate and nonparametric inference to handle uncertainties in solar PV, electricity prices, and bus behavior, validated on a 20-EB solar-powered station.
AI.motivation: To develop a flexible EMS for EBCS that effectively handles multiple uncertainties (solar PV, electricity prices, EB arrival/departure SoC) while requiring only limited historical data for training.
AI.method: A data-driven polynomial chaos expansion surrogate is constructed from limited uncertainty samples, combined with a nonparametric inference method to enrich input data when historical data is scarce.
AI.result: Case studies on a solar-powered EBCS with 20 EBs demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed EMS and data-driven method.
AI.conclusion: The proposed data-driven EMS approach effectively manages charging station operations under uncertainty, even with limited historical data availability.

title: Randomized Atomic Feature Models for Physics-Informed Identification of Dynamic Systems
comment: Extended version of the conference paper submitted for IFAC World Congress, 2026
summary: We present a physics-informed framework for system identification based on randomized stable atomic features. Impulse responses are represented as random superpositions of stable atoms, namely damped complex exponentials associated with poles sampled inside a prescribed disk. Identification is then cast as a convex regularized least-squares problem with optional linear, second-order-cone, and KYP constraints. The approach generalizes random Fourier and random Laplace features to the damped, nonstationary regime relevant to engineering systems while retaining modal interpretability and scalable finite-dimensional computation. The main analytic point is an operator-theoretic Disk-Bochner viewpoint: positive measures over stable poles generate positive-definite kernels with a radius-dependent shift defect, while a converse scalar disk moment representation for an arbitrary kernel is characterized by subnormality of the canonical shift. We prove this statement, establish an RKHS-to-l1 embedding, show that sampled poles induce a valid finite atomic gauge, discuss random-feature convergence, and state sparse-recovery guarantees conditionally on the restricted-eigenvalue properties of the realized disk-Vandermonde or input-output design matrix. We also connect the normalized transfer function problem to Nevanlinna-Pick interpolation and LFT set-membership. The framework directly encodes stability margins, modal localization, DC-gain bounds, monotonicity, passivity, relative degree, settling-time targets, and time/frequency-domain error bounds. Numerical comparisons illustrate how physically meaningful priors can compensate for poor excitation and improve constrained impulse-response recovery in an under-informative data setting.

AI.tldr: A physics-informed system identification framework using randomized stable atomic features (damped complex exponentials) that casts identification as a convex regularized least-squares problem with constraints, underpinned by a Disk-Bochner theorem connecting positive measures over stable poles to positive-definite kernels with shift defects.
AI.motivation: To generalize random Fourier/Laplace features to damped, nonstationary regimes relevant to engineering systems, while preserving modal interpretability and enabling physically meaningful priors to compensate for poor excitation in under-informative data settings.
AI.method: Represents impulse responses as random superpositions of stable atoms (damped complex exponentials with poles inside a prescribed disk); formulates identification as convex regularized least-squares with linear, SOC, and KYP constraints; establishes a Disk-Bochner theorem linking positive measures to kernels with shift defects; provides RKHS-to-l1 embedding, finite atomic gauge validity, random-feature convergence, and sparse-recovery guarantees; connects to Nevanlinna-Pick interpolation and LFT set-membership.
AI.result: The framework encodes stability margins, modal localization, DC-gain bounds, monotonicity, passivity, relative degree, settling-time targets, and time/frequency-domain error bounds. Numerical comparisons show that physically meaningful priors improve constrained impulse-response recovery in under-informative data settings.
AI.conclusion: The proposed disk-Bochner viewpoint and randomized atomic feature framework provide a principled, scalable, and interpretable approach to constrained system identification that leverages physical priors to overcome data limitations.

title: Automated Curriculum Design for High-dimensional Human Motor Learning
summary: Designing effective practice schedules for high-dimensional motor learning tasks remains a challenge, especially when skill states are unobservable and task performance may not reflect the true learning. We propose an automated curriculum design framework that combines a human motor learning model and personalized real-time skill estimation with Stochastic Nonlinear Model Predictive Control in \emph{de-novo} (novel) motor learning paradigms. We validated our framework both through simulations and human-subject studies (N = 36) using a hand exoskeleton. Our proposed approach accelerates skill acquisition by $\sim23\%$, and ${\sim17\%}$ when compared to a random curriculum and a performance heuristics-based curriculum, respectively. These significant gains in learning efficiency highlight the potential of model-based, individualized curricula for motor rehabilitation and complex skill training.

AI.tldr: An automated curriculum design framework combining a human motor learning model with Stochastic Nonlinear Model Predictive Control and real-time skill estimation accelerates skill acquisition by 23% and 17% over random and performance-heuristic curricula, respectively, validated via simulations and a 36-subject hand exoskeleton study.
AI.motivation: Designing effective practice schedules for high-dimensional motor learning is challenging due to unobservable skill states and the disconnect between task performance and true learning.
AI.method: A framework integrating a human motor learning model with personalized real-time skill estimation and Stochastic Nonlinear Model Predictive Control in de-novo motor learning paradigms, validated through simulations and a 36-subject hand exoskeleton study.
AI.result: ~23% faster skill acquisition versus random curriculum and ~17% faster versus performance heuristics-based curriculum.
AI.conclusion: Model-based, individualized curricula have strong potential for accelerating motor rehabilitation and complex skill training.

title: Fully Dynamic Rebalancing in Dockless Bike-Sharing Systems via Deep Reinforcement Learning
comment: 6 pages, 5 figures, 1 table, accepted at the 23rd IFAC World Congress, Busan, South Korea, Aug. 23-26, 2026. Open invited track 9-131: "Control and Optimization for Smart Cities"
summary: This paper proposes a fully dynamic Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) method for rebalancing dockless bike-sharing systems, overcoming the limitations of periodic, system-wide interventions. We model the service through a graph-based simulator and cast rebalancing as a Markov decision process. A DRL agent routes a single truck in real time, executing localized pick-up, drop-off, and charging actions guided by spatiotemporal criticality scores. Experiments on real-world data show significant reductions in availability failures with a minimal fleet size, while limiting spatial inequality and mobility deserts. Our approach demonstrates the value of learning-based rebalancing for efficient and reliable shared micromobility.

AI.tldr: A fully dynamic DRL method for real-time rebalancing of dockless bike-sharing systems, using a single truck guided by spatiotemporal criticality scores, achieving significant reductions in availability failures with minimal fleet size.
AI.motivation: Overcoming the limitations of periodic, system-wide interventions for rebalancing dockless bike-sharing systems.
AI.method: Models the service as a graph-based simulator; casts rebalancing as a Markov decision process; a DRL agent routes a single truck in real time with localized pick-up, drop-off, and charging actions based on spatiotemporal criticality scores.
AI.result: Significant reductions in availability failures with a minimal fleet size, while limiting spatial inequality and mobility deserts on real-world data.
AI.conclusion: Learning-based rebalancing is valuable for efficient and reliable shared micromobility.

title: Quantifying Cyber-Vulnerability in Power Electronics Systems via an Impedance-Based Attack Reachable Domain
summary: Power electronics systems are increasingly exposed to cyber threats due to their integration with digital controllers and communication networks. However, an attacker-oriented metric is still lacking to quantify the extent to which a node can be pushed toward instability within a privilege-constrained action space. This letter proposes an impedance-based Attack Reachable Domain (ARD) framework that maps feasible adversarial actions to critical-eigenvalue migration through impedance reshaping. Based on the ARD, an Attack Penetration Index is defined to quantify node-level cyber-vulnerability by jointly characterizing the penetration of the nominal stability margin and the accessibility of successful destabilizing attacks within a privilege-constrained action space. To make the proposed assessment computable when inverter models are unavailable, a practical gray-box workflow is further established by integrating existing impedance identification and differentiable surrogate tools. Case studies on a 4-bus system and a modified IEEE 39-bus system show that coordinated cross-layer manipulations are markedly more damaging than isolated single-layer attacks, and that the proposed metric reveals vulnerability patterns that cannot be inferred from grid-strength indicators.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes an Attack Reachable Domain (ARD) framework and Attack Penetration Index (API) to quantify node-level cyber-vulnerability in power electronics systems under privilege-constrained attacks, using impedance-based analysis and a gray-box workflow for practical assessment.
AI.motivation: Existing metrics lack attacker-oriented quantification of how much a node can be pushed toward instability within a privilege-constrained action space; there is no impedance-based framework to map adversarial actions to stability margins.
AI.method: An impedance-based Attack Reachable Domain (ARD) framework is proposed that maps feasible adversarial actions to critical-eigenvalue migration via impedance reshaping. An Attack Penetration Index (API) is defined to quantify node-level vulnerability by jointly characterizing nominal stability margin penetration and accessibility of successful destabilizing attacks. A gray-box workflow integrates impedance identification and differentiable surrogate models when inverter models are unavailable.
AI.result: Case studies on a 4-bus system and modified IEEE 39-bus system show that coordinated cross-layer manipulations are markedly more damaging than isolated single-layer attacks, and the proposed metric reveals vulnerability patterns not inferable from conventional grid-strength indicators.
AI.conclusion: The ARD framework and API metric provide a novel attacker-oriented perspective for quantifying cyber-vulnerability in power electronics systems, highlighting the heightened risk of coordinated cross-layer attacks and uncovering blind spots of traditional grid-strength-based assessments.

title: Admittance-Guided Inverter Dispatch Command Manipulation Attack: A Grid Stability-Oriented Approach
summary: The high penetration of voltage source converters in modern smart microgrids enhances operational flexibility while introducing complex cyber-physical vulnerabilities. Existing cyber-attack studies either require detailed knowledge of system topology and controller dynamics or depend on repeated online interactions, which may compromise practicality by generating operationally infeasible or limit-violating commands. This article investigates a dispatch command manipulation attack and develops an admittance-guided framework to identify the vulnerable inverter and the worst-case dispatch command that most severely degrades system stability. A compromised inverter is utilized to inject controlled harmonic perturbations for sparse admittance measurement, and a physics-informed neural network is then employed to reconstruct the operating-point-dependent admittance of target inverters over the feasible dispatch region. Based on the reconstructed admittance, a stability-margin-oriented optimization is formulated to locate the most vulnerable inverter and the corresponding worst-case dispatch command. Controller hardware-in-the-loop experiments on a five-inverter microgrid demonstrate that the identified command can drive the system into severe sub-synchronous oscillations while remaining within nominal dispatch bounds, highlighting the need for stability-aware command screening beyond static limit checking.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates a dispatch command manipulation attack in microgrids with high inverter penetration. It develops an admittance-guided framework that uses sparse harmonic perturbations and a physics-informed neural network to reconstruct operating-point-dependent admittance, then identifies the most vulnerable inverter and worst-case dispatch command that degrades system stability while staying within nominal limits.
AI.motivation: Existing cyber-attack studies require detailed knowledge of system topology/controller dynamics or depend on repeated online interactions, generating operationally infeasible or limit-violating commands. The authors aim to develop a more practical attack identification framework.
AI.method: (1) A compromised inverter injects controlled harmonic perturbations for sparse admittance measurement. (2) A physics-informed neural network reconstructs the operating-point-dependent admittance of target inverters over the feasible dispatch region. (3) A stability-margin-oriented optimization locates the most vulnerable inverter and corresponding worst-case dispatch command.
AI.result: Controller hardware-in-the-loop experiments on a five-inverter microgrid show that the identified command drives the system into severe sub-synchronous oscillations while remaining within nominal dispatch bounds.
AI.conclusion: There is a need for stability-aware command screening beyond static limit checking to protect against such covert cyber-physical attacks.

title: Distributionally Robust Model Predictive Control for Virtual Power Plants
comment: 7 pages, 5 figures, submitted to IFAC World Congress 2026
summary: This paper presents a distributionally robust model predictive control (DRMPC) framework for the optimal Virtual Power Plant (VPP) operation under electricity price uncertainty. A unified VPP model is formulated that captures the interaction between buildings, battery storage, and renewable generation, all influenced by exogenous weather and market signals. The proposed approach integrates data-driven forecasting with quantile-based uncertainty quantification to construct time-varying Wasserstein ambiguity sets that adapt to forecast dispersion and distributional shifts. This yields a tractable DR-MPC formulation that incorporates predictive distribution information directly into real-time decision making. The method is evaluated using real weather and market data from a Nordic case study across two seasonal scenarios. The results show that DR-MPC improves economic performance relative to standard forecast-based MPC when the ambiguity radius is chosen appropriately, with consistent gains of up to 0.8% for small radii across both seasonal scenarios. Larger radii become overly conservative and reduce revenue, underscoring the importance of proper radius selection. These findings demonstrate the practical value of distributionally robust optimization for uncertainty-aware VPP operation.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a distributionally robust MPC framework for Virtual Power Plant operation that uses time-varying Wasserstein ambiguity sets based on forecast dispersion to handle electricity price uncertainty, showing up to 0.8% economic improvement over standard MPC in a Nordic case study.
AI.motivation: Electricity price uncertainty poses a significant challenge for optimal VPP operation, and traditional forecast-based MPC methods lack robustness against distributional shifts and forecast errors.
AI.method: The authors formulate a unified VPP model integrating buildings, battery storage, and renewables; then develop a DR-MPC framework that uses data-driven forecasting with quantile-based uncertainty quantification to construct time-varying Wasserstein ambiguity sets that adapt to forecast dispersion and distributional shifts.
AI.result: DR-MPC achieves up to 0.8% economic improvement over standard MPC for small ambiguity radii across both seasonal scenarios; larger radii become overly conservative and reduce revenue.
AI.conclusion: Distributionally robust optimization provides practical value for uncertainty-aware VPP operation, but proper ambiguity radius selection is critical to avoid excessive conservatism.

title: Dynamic Event-Triggered Control of Discrete-Time Nonlinear Systems based on Difference-Algebraic Representations
comment: Accepted to the IFAC World Congress 2026
summary: This paper addresses the dynamic event-triggered control for a class of discrete-time nonlinear systems described by a difference-algebraic representation (DAR), using a gain-scheduled controller. An outstanding aspect of the proposed method is the incorporation of information about the system's nonlinearities into the control law and the trigger function. The proposed event-triggered mechanism also incorporates information on the asynchronous terms induced by the event-based sampling. All these ingredients enable the derivation of a less conservative co-design condition for the simultaneous design of the gain-scheduled control law and the dynamic triggering mechanism to ensure the asymptotic stability of the closed-loop system. An estimate of the region of attraction of the origin of the closed-loop system is obtained to guarantee the closed-loop system's operation within the domain of validity of the DAR. Then, an optimization problem is formulated to reduce the number of events and enlarge the estimated region of attraction. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed condition is illustrated by a numerical example.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a less conservative co-design method for dynamic event-triggered control of discrete-time nonlinear systems (via DAR) using a gain-scheduled controller, incorporating nonlinearity and asynchrony information to jointly design the control law and trigger mechanism while ensuring asymptotic stability and enlarging the region of attraction.
AI.motivation: To address the conservatism in existing event-triggered control designs for discrete-time nonlinear systems by incorporating nonlinearity information and asynchronous terms into both the control law and trigger function, enabling a less restrictive co-design condition.
AI.method: The method models nonlinear systems using a difference-algebraic representation (DAR), designs a gain-scheduled controller, and formulates a dynamic event-triggered mechanism that accounts for asynchronous terms. A co-design condition is derived to simultaneously synthesize the controller and trigger law, with an optimization problem to reduce event frequency and enlarge the estimated region of attraction.
AI.result: A less conservative co-design condition is derived that ensures asymptotic stability of the closed-loop system, with an optimized trade-off between reducing the number of triggered events and enlarging the estimated region of attraction, validated via a numerical example.
AI.conclusion: The proposed approach effectively reduces conservatism in dynamic event-triggered control for discrete-time nonlinear systems by leveraging DAR and gain-scheduled co-design, and demonstrates practical feasibility through numerical validation.

title: Flexibility-Aware Framework for Efficient Planner-Initiated Siting of Data Center
comment: Accepted for publication in Nature Communications. 33 pages, 4 figures
summary: Explosive growth in energy-intensive AI data centers is outstripping the pace of power grid interconnection and transmission expansion. While operational flexibility has been proposed to mitigate this stress, existing processes are often reactive and evaluate projects only after they enter a multi-year interconnection queue. To address this, we introduce a planner-initiated siting framework that integrates (i) reliability-gated screening, (ii) system-wide market-impact assessment under standardized flexibility envelopes (firm, pause, and shift), and (iii) entropy-weighted multi-criteria scoring to produce ranked, pre-certified catalogues of interconnection-ready locations. Applied to a synthetic 2,000-bus Texas power system, the framework demonstrates that operational flexibility expands the siting frontier by 9-17% at 1 GW and 19-21% at 2 GW compared to firm operation. Median all-hour average prices remain essentially unchanged (USD 24.32/MWh for the 2 GW cases), and the shift envelope attenuates peak-hour price dispersion by approximately 3.4% with minimal side effects during off-peak hours. Utilizing pre-certified envelopes to bypass major transmission reinforcements, this workflow enables first energization in 12-18 months, a conservative reduction of 3.5-4 years versus the conventional 5-8 year project-led process. This technology-agnostic framework provides a proactive decision-making tool for system operators and regulators to fast-track large flexible loads while preserving grid reliability and market stability.

AI.tldr: A planner-initiated siting framework integrating reliability-gated screening, market-impact assessment under flexibility envelopes, and entropy-weighted multi-criteria scoring is proposed to fast-track interconnection-ready locations for large flexible AI data center loads, demonstrating 9-21% expansion of the siting frontier and reducing energization timelines from 5-8 years to 12-18 months on a synthetic 2,000-bus Texas system.
AI.motivation: Energy-intensive AI data centers are growing faster than power grid interconnection and transmission expansion can accommodate, and existing reactive project-led evaluation processes cause multi-year delays.
AI.method: The framework consists of three stages: (i) reliability-gated screening to filter candidate locations, (ii) system-wide market-impact assessment under three standardized flexibility envelopes (firm, pause, and shift), and (iii) entropy-weighted multi-criteria scoring to produce ranked, pre-certified catalogues of interconnection-ready locations. Validation is conducted on a synthetic 2,000-bus Texas power system.
AI.result: Operational flexibility expands the siting frontier by 9-17% at 1 GW and 19-21% at 2 GW versus firm operation. Median all-hour average prices remain ~USD 24.32/MWh for 2 GW cases. The shift envelope reduces peak-hour price dispersion by ~3.4% with minimal off-peak side effects. First energization is achievable in 12-18 months, a 3.5-4 year reduction versus the conventional 5-8 year process.
AI.conclusion: The proposed technology-agnostic, proactive framework enables system operators and regulators to fast-track large flexible loads while preserving grid reliability and market stability.

title: Addressing Terminal Constraints in Data-Driven Demand Response Scheduling
summary: Electrified chemical processes are incentivized by exposure to time-varying electricity markets to operate flexibly, but participating in demand response schemes can require satisfying terminal constraints over long horizons. Specifically, terminal constraints may be required when computing optimal schedules in order to preserve dynamic stability. Model-based optimization methods are computationally costly, and data-driven scheduling via reinforcement learning (RL) faces severe credit-assignment challenges. We integrate Goal-Space Planning (GSP) with Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG), using learned temporally abstract models over discrete subgoals to propagate value across extended horizons. Using a simulated air separation benchmark, we demonstrate the proposed approach improves sample efficiency over standard DDPG while satisfying terminal storage constraints, mitigating myopic control behavior.

AI.tldr: Integration of Goal-Space Planning with Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient improves sample efficiency and satisfies terminal storage constraints in electrified chemical process scheduling under time-varying electricity markets.
AI.motivation: Electrified chemical processes face challenges in demand response due to terminal constraints over long horizons needed for dynamic stability, with model-based methods being computationally costly and RL suffering from credit-assignment issues.
AI.method: Integrates Goal-Space Planning (GSP) with Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG), using learned temporally abstract models over discrete subgoals to propagate value across extended horizons.
AI.result: On a simulated air separation benchmark, the proposed approach improves sample efficiency over standard DDPG while satisfying terminal storage constraints and mitigating myopic control behavior.
AI.conclusion: Goal-Space Planning combined with DDPG effectively addresses long-horizon credit assignment and terminal constraint satisfaction in electrified chemical process scheduling under dynamic electricity pricing.

title: Hybrid Metaheuristic Optimization of Distributed Control System Hardware Architecture with Model-Based Verification
summary: Large-scale chemical plants rely on distributed process control systems (PCS) comprising numerous processing units, communication modules, and I/O devices interconnected via industrial networks. The design of a cost-efficient and reliable hardware architecture under partial uncertainty in plant parameters remains a challenging combinatorial optimization problem. This paper proposes a formal model for distributed control system hardware architecture synthesis. A hybrid ant colony-based metaheuristic framework is developed to construct feasible hierarchical architectures. The proposed approach is validated on a large-scale sulfuric acid plant control system case study. Plant parameters are identified from operational data, system stability is analyzed, and a controller synthesis is performed based on the optimized architecture. The results demonstrate the feasibility of the approach and confirm that the obtained architecture satisfies structural and dynamic performance requirements.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a formal model and hybrid ant colony-based metaheuristic for synthesizing cost-efficient and reliable hardware architectures of distributed process control systems under parameter uncertainty, validated on a large-scale sulfuric acid plant case study.
AI.motivation: The design of cost-efficient and reliable hardware architectures for large-scale chemical plant control systems under partial parameter uncertainty is a challenging combinatorial optimization problem that has not been adequately addressed.
AI.method: A formal model for distributed control system hardware architecture synthesis is proposed, along with a hybrid ant colony-based metaheuristic framework to construct feasible hierarchical architectures.
AI.result: Validated on a large-scale sulfuric acid plant case study. Plant parameters identified from operational data, system stability analyzed, and controller synthesized based on optimized architecture. The architecture satisfies structural and dynamic performance requirements.
AI.conclusion: The approach is feasible and the obtained architecture meets both structural and dynamic performance requirements for large-scale chemical plant control systems.

title: Robust Quadcopter Motion Control Using Output Feedback
summary: The study addresses the problem of quadcopter motion control using output feedback. By applying a geometric approach, the quadcopter model is transformed into a normal form with a time-varying gain coefficient, which is subsequently made stationary through double integration of the control input. A robust output feedback control law is synthesised based on the extended observer method.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a robust output feedback control law for quadcopter motion control, using a geometric approach to transform the model into a normal form with a time-varying gain coefficient, which is then stabilized via double integration of the control input, and synthesized using the extended observer method.
AI.motivation: To address the problem of quadcopter motion control when only output feedback (not full state) is available, which is more practical for real-world applications.
AI.method: A geometric approach is applied to transform the quadcopter model into a normal form with a time-varying gain coefficient; the gain is then made stationary via double integration of the control input; a robust output feedback control law is synthesized using the extended observer method.
AI.result: A robust output feedback control law is developed that can handle the time-varying gain coefficient and achieve stable quadcopter motion control.
AI.conclusion: The proposed method successfully enables quadcopter motion control using only output feedback, offering a practical solution for real-world deployment.

title: On the Nonexistence of Continuous Immersions for Discrete-time Systems
comment: Copyright 2026 the authors. This work has been accepted to IFAC 2026 for publication under a Creative Commons License CC-BY-NC-ND
summary: Understanding when linear immersions of nonlinear dynamical systems exist is important since such immersions allow us to leverage the rich tools of linear system theory to analyze nonlinear dynamics. Recently, Liu et al. (2023) showed that continuous-time dynamical systems that admit countably many but more than one omega-limit sets cannot be immersed into finite dimensional linear systems with a one-to-one and continuous mapping. In this paper, we extend these results to discrete-time dynamics and show that similar obstructions exist also in discrete time. We further consider a generalization involving alpha-limit sets. Several examples are provided to demonstrate the results.

AI.tldr: This paper proves that discrete-time nonlinear dynamical systems with multiple omega-limit sets cannot be immersed into finite-dimensional linear systems via continuous injective mappings, extending prior continuous-time results, and generalizes the obstruction to alpha-limit sets.
AI.motivation: Understanding when nonlinear systems can be linearly immersed (embedded into linear systems) is important for applying linear system theory tools to nonlinear dynamics. Prior work (Liu et al., 2023) identified obstructions in continuous-time; this paper extends that analysis to discrete-time systems.
AI.method: The paper extends the continuous-time obstruction results of Liu et al. (2023) to discrete-time dynamical systems. It formally shows that systems with countably many (more than one) omega-limit sets cannot be immersed into finite-dimensional linear systems using one-to-one continuous mappings. It further generalizes the analysis to alpha-limit sets and provides illustrative examples.
AI.result: The obstruction (non-existence of finite-dimensional linear immersions via continuous injective mappings) holds for discrete-time systems with multiple omega-limit sets, mirroring the continuous-time case. The result is also generalized to alpha-limit sets.
AI.conclusion: Discrete-time nonlinear dynamical systems with more than one omega-limit set cannot be immersed into finite-dimensional linear systems via continuous one-to-one mappings. This extends known continuous-time obstructions to the discrete-time setting, and the generalization to alpha-limit sets further broadens the applicability of these impossibility results.
